'''''Cressa cretica''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Convolvulaceae|morning glory family]]. It is found in northern and central Africa, southern Europe and western Asia, as well as parts of southeastern Asia and Australia. It has long been used in traditional medicine and research has demonstrated that it has some therapeutic effects.

==Description==
''Cressa cretica'' is a densely branching subshrub growing to a height of about {{convert|38|cm|in|0|abbr=on}}. The leaves are small, stubby, obtuse and clad in silky hairs. The flowers grow in groups in the axils of the upper leaves and are white; the back of the reflexed corolla lobes are hairy near the tip. The fruits are ovoid, pointed capsules, usually containing a single seed.<ref name=Compendium>{{cite book|title=Indian Medicinal Plants: A Compendium of 500 Species|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uDzsHbrVV-UC&pg=PA206 |year=1997|publisher=Orient Blackswan|isbn=978-81-250-0246-8|page=206}}</ref>

==Etymology==
Cressa: Greek, based on kris or kriti, "from Crete", a Cretan woman.<ref name=etymology>{{Cite journal | author = DANIEL FAUSTIN | title = ''Cressa cretica'' | journal = [[Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society]] | volume = 113 | pages = 27–39 | publisher = [[IUCN]] | date = 2010 | doi = 10.1006/bojl.1999.0326 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Cressa cretica'' is known from the Mediterranean part of Europe, northern and central Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, the Middle East and western Asia as far east as India and Sri Lanka. It also occurs in parts of southeastern Asia and in a number of states in Australia, but it is unclear as to whether it is native to these places. It is a [[halophyte]] and grows in salty parts of [[Oasis|oases]], in depressions in sandy areas that become wet seasonally, in [[salt marsh]]es and beside temporary pools.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />

==Uses==
This plant is much used in [[traditional medicine]]; it is reputed to be an anthelmintic, an expectorant, an aid to digestion, an aphrodisiac and to have tonic properties among other uses.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" /><ref name=Compendium/> Research shows that the plant contains a number of chemical constituents and that it has some potential as an [[Antibiotics|antibacterial]], an [[antifungal]] and an [[Cough medicine|antitussive]] agent. In combination with ''[[Tridax procumbens]]'' and ''[[Euphorbia thymifolia]]'', it has been found to be effective as an anticancer treatment. It has also been shown to improve testicular function in rats.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Priyashree, S. |author2=Jha, S. |author3=Pattanayak, S.P. |year=2010 |title=A review on ''Cressa cretica'' Linn.: A halophytic plant |journal=Pharmacognosy Reviews |volume=4 |issue=8 |pages=161–166 |doi=10.4103/0973-7847.70910 |pmid=22228956 |pmc=3249916 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
